generalfeedback:
If \(u\) and \(v\) are both functions of {{CT:1}} then \[\int u dv = uv - \int v du.\]

Let \(u = {{CT:2}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:3}} d{{CT:4}}\).

Then \(du = {{CT:5}} d{{CT:4}}\) and \(v = {{CT:6}}\).

So,
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:2}}{{CT:6}} - \int {{CT:6}}{{CT:5}}d{{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}} - \int {{CT:9}}d{{CT:4}}
 \end{array}\]

To calculate \[\int {{CT:9}}d{{CT:4}}\] we will have to use parts again, by defining

\(u = {{CT:10}}\) and \(dv = {{CT:11}}d{{CT:4}}\) so that

\(du = {{CT:12}}d{{CT:4}}\) and \(v = {{CT:13}}\).

So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:9}}d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int u dv \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  uv - \int v du \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:10}}{{CT:13}} - \int {{CT:13}}{{CT:12}}d{{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:14}} - \int {{CT:15}}d{{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:16}} + c
 \end{array}\]

Hence,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:4}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}} - \int {{CT:9}}d{{CT:4}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:8}} - \left({{CT:17}}\right) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:18}}
 \end{array}\]
